intro: Excerpts copied from the live PersonalSong source (C:\PersonalSong). Each shows the real code behind a capability and explains how it powers that feature. The creative core is local + free: Ollama for lyrics, ACE-Step for sung vocals, Demucs + Seed-VC for voice cloning, edge-tts for dedications. No model names or paths are guessed here — they are read straight from the files.

snippets.title: FFmpeg DLLs on PATH before anything else
snippets.feature: torchcodec / Demucs / Seed-VC can load on Windows
snippets.code:
FFMPEG_BIN = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    / "ffmpeg_shared" / "v71"
    / "ffmpeg-n7.1-latest-win64-gpl-shared-7.1" / "bin"
)

def ensure_ffmpeg_on_path() -> str:
    p = str(FFMPEG_BIN)
    cur = os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    if p.lower() not in cur.lower():
        os.environ["PATH"] = p + os.pathsep + cur
    return p

# Apply on import for convenience.
ensure_ffmpeg_on_path()
snippets.explanation: On torch 2.11, torchaudio routes through TorchCodec, which needs FFmpeg *shared* DLLs absent from a stock Windows box. This vendored FFmpeg 7.1 build is prepended to PATH on import; subprocesses (Demucs, Seed-VC) inherit it, so they don't fail with 'libtorchcodec_core7.dll could not be loaded'. Every entry point imports env_setup first.

snippets.title: App + 12 routers under /api/*
snippets.feature: FastAPI web app on port 8088
snippets.code:
import env_setup  # noqa: F401  -> puts FFmpeg shared DLLs on PATH for torchcodec
load_dotenv()
Path("music_library").mkdir(exist_ok=True)

from routers import (audio, batch, config_api, extras, library, lyrics,
                     media, prompt_api, source_api, voices, ytmusic_api)

app = FastAPI(title="PersonalSong Studio", version="2.2.0")
app.include_router(lyrics.router, prefix="/api/lyrics", tags=["Lyrics"])
app.include_router(audio.router, prefix="/api/audio", tags=["Audio"])
app.include_router(source_api.router, prefix="/api/source", tags=["Source"])
# ... library, config, media, extras, voices, batch, prompt, ytmusic
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")
snippets.explanation: The single FastAPI app. env_setup is imported FIRST (PATH side-effect), then the routers are mounted under /api/*. The static single-page studio is served at / and /static. One health route returns {status: ok}. Every heavy capability lives behind one of these routers.

snippets.title: Run uvicorn IN-PROCESS so acestep resolves
snippets.feature: Service uses the venv that has the singing model
snippets.explanation: 'python -m uvicorn' spawned a child process that resolved to the base Python (no acestep) and broke song generation. serve.py calls uvicorn.run() in-process so the server stays in the venv that has acestep, and asserts the import up front so a misconfigured environment fails loudly instead of at first generation. This is what PersonalSong_Install.bat runs as QI_PersonalSong.

snippets.title: think=False + keep_alive=0
snippets.feature: Local LLM emits lyrics directly and frees the GPU
snippets.code:
resp = await client.post(
    f"{OLLAMA_BASE_URL}/api/generate",
    json={
        "model": OLLAMA_MODEL,
        "prompt": prompt,
        "stream": False,
        # think=False -> qwen3 emits lyrics directly instead of burning the
        # token budget on internal reasoning (which returns an EMPTY response).
        "think": False,
        # keep_alive=0 -> Ollama unloads the model from VRAM right after,
        # freeing the GPU for ACE-Step music generation.
        "keep_alive": 0,
        "options": {"temperature": 0.85, "top_p": 0.9, "num_predict": 900},
    },
)
snippets.explanation: Two of the project's defining gotchas in one call. think=False stops reasoning models like qwen3 from spending their whole budget on a hidden <think> block and returning empty lyrics. keep_alive=0 tells Ollama to unload immediately so the single GPU is free for ACE-Step, which runs right after.

snippets.title: Force the name to be sung, at least twice
snippets.feature: The recipient's name is reliably in the song
snippets.code:
lines += [
    f"Music genre: {genre_str}",
    f"Mood / tempo: {r.mood}",
    f"Vocal style: {r.vocal_preference}",
    f"Target length: about {int(r.duration or 45)} seconds ...",
    "",
    "Write the full song with these clearly labelled sections ...",
] + structure + [
    "",
    f"Rules: The name '{r.recipient_name}' MUST appear, written EXACTLY as '{r.recipient_name}' "
    f"(never translated or transliterated), AT LEAST TWICE — including in the chorus — so it is clearly heard when sung.",
    "Keep each line short and singable (6-10 words). ...",
    "Output ONLY the lyrics with section labels. No intro, no commentary, no explanations.",
]
snippets.explanation: The prompt is engineered for a singable, personal result: a duration-scaled section layout, short lines, and a hard rule that the exact name appears at least twice including the chorus. 'Output ONLY the lyrics' keeps the model from wrapping the song in chatty commentary that would otherwise be sung.

snippets.title: Lazy singleton pipeline (bf16, auto-download)
snippets.feature: Sung-vocal model loaded once, kept in VRAM
snippets.code:
def get_pipeline():
    """Lazy-load the ACE-Step pipeline once and keep it resident."""
    global _pipeline
    if _pipeline is None:
        with _lock:
            if _pipeline is None:
                _patch_torchaudio_save()
                from acestep.pipeline_ace_step import ACEStepPipeline
                _pipeline = ACEStepPipeline(
                    checkpoint_dir=None,        # auto-download to ~/.cache/ace-step
                    dtype="bfloat16",
                    torch_compile=False,
                    cpu_offload=False,
                    overlapped_decode=False,
                )
    return _pipeline
snippets.explanation: ACE-Step is expensive to load, so it is built once behind a double-checked lock and kept resident in VRAM for every request. Weights auto-download on first use; bfloat16 fits the local GPU. _patch_torchaudio_save() is applied first so the model writes audio via soundfile instead of the missing TorchCodec FFmpeg path.

snippets.title: The generate_song call into ACE-Step
snippets.feature: Full sung song from lyrics + style tags
snippets.code:
pipe = get_pipeline()
a2a = bool(ref_audio_input) and ref_audio_strength > 0.01
pipe(
    audio_duration=duration,
    prompt=tags,
    lyrics=lyrics,
    infer_step=infer_step,            # 60
    guidance_scale=guidance_scale,    # 7.5
    scheduler_type="euler",
    cfg_type="apg",
    omega_scale=10.0,
    manual_seeds=seed,
    use_erg_tag=True, use_erg_lyric=True, use_erg_diffusion=True,
    audio2audio_enable=a2a,
    ref_audio_strength=float(ref_audio_strength),
    ref_audio_input=ref_audio_input if a2a else None,
    save_path=save_path,
)
return save_path
snippets.explanation: The single call that performs the song. tags is the style prompt, lyrics carries the [verse]/[chorus] structure with the name. When a reference song and a non-zero strength are supplied, audio2audio is enabled so the new song is steered by an existing one ('base it on a song'); otherwise it generates fresh from the prompt + lyrics.

snippets.title: Bypass TorchCodec — write WAV via soundfile
snippets.feature: Audio saves on Windows without FFmpeg shared DLLs
snippets.code:
import soundfile as sf
import torchaudio

def _sf_save(filepath, src, sample_rate, *args, **kwargs):
    arr = src.detach().cpu().to(torch.float32).numpy() if hasattr(src, "detach") else src
    if arr.ndim == 2:          # torchaudio is (channels, samples) -> sf wants (samples, channels)
        arr = arr.T
    sf.write(str(filepath), arr, int(sample_rate))

torchaudio.save = _sf_save
snippets.explanation: ACE-Step saves via torchaudio.save(), which on torch 2.11 routes through TorchCodec -> FFmpeg shared DLLs that aren't present. The monkey-patch swaps in a soundfile writer (libsndfile is bundled, no external FFmpeg), transposing the channel layout torchaudio uses to what soundfile expects.

snippets.title: Build the ACE style prompt (gender first)
snippets.feature: Genre/mood/language/singer -> ACE tags
snippets.code:
parts = [
    _VOCAL_TAGS.get(vocal, ""),             # gender FIRST so it's weighted strongly
    genre_tag,
    voice_descriptor,                       # specific singer timbre, if chosen
    _MOOD_TAGS.get(mood, mood.lower()),
    lang_tag,
    "studio quality, clear vocals",
]
return ", ".join(p for p in parts if p)
snippets.explanation: Composes the prompt ACE-Step conditions on. Vocal gender is placed first so it weighs heavily; then curated genre tags (incl. Brazilian, Japanese and French styles), the chosen singer's timbre descriptor, mood, and native-language conditioning. Genres and languages may be lists, supporting blended-genre and blended-language songs.

snippets.title: Inject the name as a sung vocative
snippets.feature: Guarantee the name is sung even if the LLM omits it
snippets.code:
for line in lines:
    st = line.strip()
    if re.match(r"^\[.*\]$", st):
        out.append(line)
        pending_section = st.lower()
        continue
    if st and pending_section in target_sections and injected < 2:
        first = st[0].lower() + st[1:] if len(st) > 1 else st
        out.append(f"{name}, {first}")
        injected += 1
        pending_section = None
        continue
    out.append(line)
...
if injected == 0:
    out.append("[chorus]")
    out.append(f"{name}, {name}, this song is for you")
snippets.explanation: LLMs writing in non-English languages often address the person without ever using their literal name, defeating the gift. If the name is absent, it's injected as a vocative ('Name, ...') into the chorus and first verse — natural in every language. If the lyrics have no usable content line at all, a sung hook with the name is appended as a last resort.

snippets.title: Respell the name only in the sung text
snippets.feature: Pronounce the name correctly without changing the lyrics
snippets.explanation: Keeps two versions of the lyrics: the display/saved copy shows the real name, while the copy fed to ACE-Step substitutes the phonetic respelling so the model sings it correctly. The audio router computes display_lyrics first, then applies the respelling only to what the model receives.

snippets.title: Verify the sung gender by pitch
snippets.feature: Gender-locked generation with retry
snippets.code:
import source_engine
# CPU so the gender check never competes with the resident ACE-Step for VRAM
stems = source_engine.separate_stems(Path(audio_path), device="cpu")
src = str(stems["vocals"])
...
y, sr = librosa.load(src, sr=22050, mono=True, duration=30)
f0, _, _ = librosa.pyin(y, fmin=80, fmax=500, sr=sr)
f0 = f0[~np.isnan(f0)]
med = float(np.median(f0))
if med >= 178: return "female"
if med <= 168: return "male"
return "female" if med >= 173 else "male"
snippets.explanation: ACE-Step's gender tag alone is unreliable, so the output is checked: Demucs isolates the vocal (forced to CPU so it doesn't steal VRAM from the resident ACE-Step), librosa estimates median pitch, and the result is classified male/female. The audio router (_generate_sync) uses this to retry once with a fresh random seed when the wrong gender comes out, bounded to two tries.

snippets.title: Serialize ACE-Step off the event loop; free Ollama first
snippets.feature: One generation at a time, GPU freed before it runs
snippets.code:
# ACE-Step generation is GPU-bound; serialize so two requests never fight the GPU.
_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
...
await _free_ollama_vram()
want_gender = vocal if vocal in ("Male", "Female") else ""
loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
await loop.run_in_executor(
    _executor, _generate_sync, tags, lyrics, str(audio_path), req.duration, seed, want_gender
)
snippets.explanation: ACE-Step is blocking and GPU-bound, so it runs in a single-worker thread pool — two concurrent requests queue instead of thrashing the one GPU. Just before, _free_ollama_vram() asks Ollama to unload its model so the full card is available. The call is run_in_executor so the async event loop stays responsive.

snippets.title: Optional steps never fail the song
snippets.feature: Resilient Plex / YouTube Music side-effects
snippets.explanation: Plex sync and YouTube Music upload are best-effort: both are wrapped so any failure (no Plex token, offline account, missing dep) is swallowed. The user always gets their finished song; the publish steps are bonuses, not blockers. The same pattern guards the spoken dedication and MP3 transcode.

snippets.title: Demucs two-stem separation as a subprocess
snippets.feature: Split vocals from instrumental
snippets.code:
cmd = [
    VENV_PY, "-m", "demucs",
    "--two-stems", "vocals",
    "-n", "htdemucs",
    "-o", str(out_root),
    "-d", device,
    str(audio_path),
]
subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, env=os.environ.copy())
# Demucs writes <out_root>/htdemucs/<trackname>/{vocals,no_vocals}.wav
vocals = track / "vocals.wav"
instrumental = track / "no_vocals.wav"
return {"vocals": vocals, "instrumental": instrumental}
snippets.explanation: Demucs (htdemucs, two-stem mode) is driven as a venv subprocess and returns the isolated vocal and the instrumental. This single function powers karaoke stems, the voice-clone reference, the gender detector, and the cover backing track. device='cpu' is passed where it must not compete with a resident GPU model.

snippets.title: Extract / trim audio from any media with FFmpeg
snippets.feature: Bring-your-own audio or video source
snippets.code:
cmd = [FFMPEG_EXE, "-y"]
if start:
    cmd += ["-ss", str(start)]
cmd += ["-i", str(src)]
if duration:
    cmd += ["-t", str(duration)]
cmd += ["-vn", "-codec:a", "libmp3lame", "-b:a", bitrate, str(out)]
subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, env=os.environ.copy())
snippets.explanation: Pulls the audio track out of any uploaded video or audio file to MP3, with optional start/duration trimming — handy for grabbing just the part of a movie where the voice you want to clone is heard, without uploading the whole file. Uses the vendored FFmpeg resolved via env_setup.

snippets.title: Full cover pipeline orchestration
snippets.feature: Re-sing an ACE song in a source singer's voice
snippets.code:
# 1. Separate the source song -> reference voice + original instrumental
src_stems = source_engine.separate_stems(source_song)
# 2. Separate the ACE-Step song -> its vocals + its instrumental
ace_stems = source_engine.separate_stems(ace_song)
# 3. Convert ACE vocals to the source singer's voice
converted = seedvc_convert(ace_stems["vocals"], src_stems["vocals"], work / "vc")
# 4. Mix over the chosen backing
backing = src_stems["instrumental"] if use_original_backing else ace_stems["instrumental"]
final = mix_vocal_over_backing(converted, backing, work / f"{out_name}.wav")
snippets.explanation: The four-step cover pipeline: Demucs isolates the target singer's voice and the ACE song's voice, Seed-VC re-sings the ACE vocal in the target timbre, and the converted vocal is mixed over either the original instrumental (a true cover) or ACE-Step's own backing (keeps the new melody).

snippets.title: Seed-VC f0-conditioned conversion (singing)
snippets.feature: Pitch-aware voice conversion in an isolated venv
snippets.code:
cmd = [
    SEEDVC_PY, "inference.py",
    "--source", str(source_vocals.resolve()),
    "--target", str(reference_voice.resolve()),
    "--output", str(out_dir.resolve()),
    "--diffusion-steps", str(diffusion_steps),
    "--f0-condition", "True",                       # required for singing
    "--auto-f0-adjust", "True" if auto_f0_adjust else "False",
    "--semi-tone-shift", "0",
    "--fp16", "True",
]
subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
               cwd=str(SEEDVC_DIR), env=os.environ.copy())
snippets.explanation: Seed-VC runs from its OWN venv as a subprocess because its dependencies collide with ACE-Step's. --f0-condition True makes the conversion pitch-aware, which is essential for singing (the spoken-dedication path uses False). Running with cwd set to the seed-vc dir lets its relative configs/modules resolve.

snippets.title: Spoken dedication re-voiced as the artist
snippets.feature: Dedication in the artist's timbre
snippets.explanation: For a spoken dedication, a vocal-rich 30-second slice of the artist's song is isolated (GPU with CPU fallback) and used as the Seed-VC reference. convert() re-voices the edge-tts speech into the artist's timbre with --f0-condition False (speech, not sung), keeping the words and native pronunciation intact.

snippets.title: Render native TTS off the FastAPI loop
snippets.feature: Spoken dedication in a native voice + optional clone
snippets.code:
async def _go():
    await edge_tts.Communicate(
        text, voice, rate=pros["rate"], pitch=pros["pitch"]
    ).save(str(out_path))

# edge-tts is async; this may be called from inside FastAPI's running event
# loop, where asyncio.run() would raise. Run it in a dedicated thread.
t = threading.Thread(target=_runner); t.start(); t.join()
...
if clone_ref is not None:
    import voice_clone
    converted = voice_clone.convert(out_path, clone_ref, out_path.parent)
    AudioSegment.from_file(converted).export(out_path, format=...)
snippets.explanation: Renders the dedication with a native edge-tts neural voice at a tone/style-specific rate and pitch. Because edge-tts is async and this is called from inside FastAPI's running loop (where asyncio.run would raise), it runs in a dedicated thread. If a clone reference is supplied, the clean speech is then re-voiced into the artist's timbre before any crowd bed is added.

snippets.title: Native wording per style/language/tone
snippets.feature: Portuguese sounds Portuguese, not translated English
snippets.explanation: Dedications are authored natively per delivery style (radio DJ vs live concert), language, and tone (heartfelt/warm/festive) — not machine-translated from English — so a Brazilian voice reads genuinely Portuguese phrasing. A matching prosody preset (rate/pitch) makes the delivery fit the words; concert style also layers a synthesized crowd/applause bed.

snippets.title: Curated singer presets
snippets.feature: Pick a consistent native-language voice
snippets.code:
{ "id": "sofia",   "name": "Sofia",   "gender": "Female",
  "descriptor": "soulful expressive female voice, rich warm tone",
  "seed": "303", "languages": ["Portuguese", "Spanish"] },
{ "id": "hana",    "name": "Hana",    "gender": "Female",
  "descriptor": "delicate bright airy female voice",
  "seed": "505", "languages": ["Japanese"] }
snippets.explanation: Each singer is an ACE-Step voice preset: a timbre descriptor (fed into build_tags as voice_descriptor) plus a stable seed for a consistent character across songs, scoped to the languages it suits. The audio router resolves the chosen singer (or a per-language default) and lets the singer's gender and seed drive the generation.

snippets.title: Persistent config with safe defaults
snippets.feature: Settings survive restarts; folders auto-created
snippets.explanation: Config is JSON-backed under config/ with a thread lock so concurrent saves don't corrupt it. Only known DEFAULTS keys are accepted (ignoring stray input), and the song/source/stem folders are (re)created after every save so a path change can't leave the app writing into a missing directory. Singers, pronunciations, voices and the overnight queue are stored the same way.

snippets.title: QR greeting card that works off-device
snippets.feature: Recipient scans to play from their phone
snippets.code:
base = str(request.base_url).rstrip("/")
if "localhost" in base or "127.0.0.1" in base:
    base = f"http://{_lan_ip()}:8088"
play_url = f"{base}/api/play/{song_id}"
qr = qrcode.make(play_url)
snippets.explanation: Generates a printable card with a QR code linking to the song's mobile play page. It uses whatever host the card was opened on (a public tunnel domain or the LAN IP) and falls back to the machine's LAN IP for localhost, so the QR actually resolves for whoever scans it rather than pointing at an unreachable localhost.

snippets.title: Install as the QI_PersonalSong service
snippets.feature: Always-on background app
snippets.code:
set NSSM=C:\QIH\engine\bin\nssm.exe
set APPDIR=C:\PersonalSong
"%NSSM%" install QI_PersonalSong "C:\PersonalSong\.venv\Scripts\python.exe" serve.py
"%NSSM%" set QI_PersonalSong AppDirectory "%APPDIR%"
"%NSSM%" set QI_PersonalSong Description "PersonalSong Studio - local AI song generator web app :8088 (acestep in .venv)."
"%NSSM%" set QI_PersonalSong AppStdout "%APPDIR%\logs\service.log"
"%NSSM%" start QI_PersonalSong
snippets.explanation: Registers the studio as a QI-standard NSSM Windows service (QI_ prefix, explicit AppDirectory + Description, rotating logs) running serve.py from the venv that has acestep, using the standardized nssm.exe at C:\QIH\engine\bin. This is how the app stays available on the machine without a terminal open.
